questions.title: Feedforward control prepares the body for anticipated events
questions.subject: fnd
questions.question: Why is the feedforward mechanism in physiological control systems named this way?

options.B: It prepares the body for an anticipated change before it occurs
options.C: It reacts to environmental stimuli only after they occur
options.D: It provides negative feedback directly to a control center

explanations.A: Incorrect. Feedforward control is not specifically about inhibiting heat loss; it is a general anticipatory strategy that can apply across many physiological variables, not a thermoregulation-specific inhibitory mechanism.
explanations.B: Correct. Feedforward control acts pre-emptively, triggering a response based on a signal that predicts a disturbance is coming, before the controlled variable has actually changed — the response moves 'forward,' ahead of the anticipated event, which is exactly why it is named feedforward. This contrasts with negative feedback, which can only correct a deviation that has already occurred, not one that is merely expected.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Reacting only after a stimulus occurs describes negative feedback, the opposite pattern from feedforward, which acts in anticipation rather than in response to an already-occurred deviation.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Feedforward is a distinct control strategy from negative feedback, not a mechanism for delivering negative feedback; the two operate by different timing logic.

questions.learning_objective: Define feedforward control as an anticipatory response triggered before an expected change occurs, and contrast it with negative feedback, which corrects a deviation only after it has happened.
